verdicts.title: Quasi-matroidal classes of ordered simplicial complexes
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We introduce the notion of a quasi-matroidal class of ordered simplicial complexes: an approximation to the idea of a matroid cryptomorphism in the landscape of ordered simplicial complexes. A quasi-matroidal class contains pure shifted simplicial complexes and ordered matroid independence complexes
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses 'quasi-matroidal classes of ordered simplicial complexes' as an approximation of matroid cryptomorphism, with no mention of communication complexity, Boolean matrices, determinants, or Euler characteristic bounds.

verdicts.title: Geometric complexity theory and matrix powering
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Valiant's famous determinant versus permanent problem is the flagship problem in algebraic complexity theory. Mulmuley and Sohoni (Siam J Comput 2001, 2008) introduced geometric complexity theory, an approach to study this and related problems via algebraic geometry and representation theory. Their approach works by multiplying the permanent polynomial with a high power of a linear form (a process called padding) and then comparing the orbit closures of the determinant and the padded permanent.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns geometric complexity theory, orbit closures, and matrix powering for the determinant-vs-permanent problem, with no mention of communication complexity, matroid Euler characteristics, or Boolean matrices with bounded rows.
